classification.tone: Irreverent, fast-talking, absurdist, and comic-book heightened

evaluation.positioning_hook: A timid death-tally clerk with erased powers is dragged into a retro-futurist suicide squad and forced to discover what he can do before a regenerating British zombie tears London apart.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise is easy to sell: an office drone with hidden powers gets shoved into a monster-hunting team, and the script keeps the action/comedy promise front and center. The audience lane is clear for genre buyers who want banter, creature combat, and a misfit-team engine.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands immediately in the opening pages: Francis wakes in a ruined field, then snaps back to a bizarre logistics office where death is literally tracked on a board. By the time Doreen straps on the outburst monitor and the team is assembled, the story engine is unmistakable.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Francis has a strong underdog lane, and the team around him gives the movie a playable ensemble of distinct comic voices. The characters are vivid in scene, though the emotional architecture is still mostly built around the mission rather than deeper personal turns.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script commits to a very specific bureaucratic-afterlife-meets-monster-hunt world, with death toll spreadsheets, outburst meters, and a corporate field unit called SINON. That combination of office satire, supernatural action, and cartoonish dialogue gives it a clear point of view.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The story moves quickly from recruitment to mission to reveal, and the London fight gives the feature a clean escalation path. The momentum is strong, though the central mystery of Francis's power is carried more by momentum than by layered suspense.

resonant_originality.reasoning: A death-processing clerk who may be able to erase anything, including a regenerating monster, is a fresh and legible engine. The idea feels novel without becoming opaque, which is exactly the kind of high-concept clarity buyers can latch onto.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: Comirum has a lived-in internal logic: logistics division, field units, wrist monitors, retro-futurist weapons, and a death-toll bureaucracy that makes the supernatural feel institutional. The office, briefing room, cafeteria, and London street all suggest a larger system beyond the frame.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone is sharply defined by deadpan profanity, absurd workplace behavior, and creature-action played with comic confidence. Francis's panic, Clara's chaos, Toast's robotic contempt, and Hal's macho nonsense create a tone that is easy to recognize from a single scene.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: There are seeds of deeper identity material in Francis's erased memory flashes and the idea that his power is tied to something he cannot yet name. The feature currently plays more as a high-energy origin story than as a layered emotional mystery.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The team has real comic friction: Francis and Ploy, Doreen and Hal, Clara and Toast all generate distinct energy. The ensemble is functional and entertaining, though the movie still lives most strongly on the central recruit-and-survive engine.

casting_characteristics: Creature/monster antagonist with performance makeup or VFX
Francis requires a physically slight, anxious lead presence
Doreen reads as a strong authority role for a 30s-40s performer
Clara, Hal, Ploy, and Toast each have highly specific comic voice requirements

locations.interior_exterior_ratio: Mostly interior with one major exterior action sequence
notable_requirements: Office floor with cubicles and briefing room
London street and alleyway night exteriors

technical.vfx_details: Multicolor energy effects, Francis's eye/forehead glow and erasure beam, creature regeneration, static/glitch effects, teleportation light, and a retro-futurist device interface.
technical.sfx_needs: Practical creature makeup or prosthetics for the British zombie, weapon transformations, breakaway glass, and impact beats.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Streaming action-comedy or premium genre feature lane
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model with franchise-adjacent sequel potential if the world is expanded

cost.note: Contained interiors keep the footprint manageable, while the London night battle, creature work, and energy effects push it above micro-budget.

cast.note: The ensemble is manageable in size, but the roles depend on sharply differentiated comic performers and a lead who can carry both panic and payoff.

location.note: The script is mostly contained, but it requires multiple office interiors plus a nighttime London action sequence with rooftops, alleyways, and street coverage.

content.note: Violence, blood, profanity, drug references, and creature carnage are all present, but the material stays in a broadly commercial genre range.

rights.note: No named real people, brands, or licensed IP are referenced in the script.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The office world is the engine.
strengths.what_it_means: The death-toll logistics division, outburst monitor, and bureaucratic field assignment give the movie a built-in production identity that can be marketed as a workplace action-comedy with a supernatural twist. Buyers who want a genre piece with a clear internal system — and actors who like playing against corporate absurdity — will immediately understand the lane.
strengths.evidence: The green chalkboard tracking weekly death tolls, the wrist device measuring outbursts, and Doreen treating field deployment like an HR decision.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Francis is a clean underdog lead.
strengths.what_it_means: A lead who starts as a frightened pencil pusher and ends up firing a multicolor erasure beam gives the film a strong transformation arc that can anchor a franchise or a one-off crowd-pleaser. This is the kind of role that attracts younger male leads looking for a breakout showcase with comedy, vulnerability, and eventual power.
strengths.evidence: Francis panics through the briefing, insists he does nothing, then discovers his power by eating the hot dog and erasing the zombie.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The ensemble has distinct comic voices.
strengths.what_it_means: Hal, Clara, Ploy, Toast, and Doreen each bring a different performance lane, which makes the movie easier to package as an ensemble and gives the marketing team multiple character hooks. That kind of playable group dynamic is attractive to buyers looking for a castable genre piece with clip-friendly dialogue.
strengths.evidence: Hal's macho bragging, Clara's coke-fueled chaos, Toast's deadpan contempt, Ploy's bass-driven swagger, and Doreen's dry authority.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The monster fight has a clear escalation ladder.
strengths.what_it_means: The London sequence gives the feature a satisfying action spine: discovery, retreat, regroup, tactic, payoff. That structure is useful for a producer because it promises a contained but energetic set piece rather than an effects-heavy sprawl.
strengths.evidence: The team learns the zombie regenerates, Francis retreats to figure out his power, and the group coordinates a three-block trap to finish the kill.

strengths.what_it_means: The script knows exactly how to sound: profane, playful, and weirdly sincere beneath the jokes. That tonal confidence helps a buyer know where to place it and helps a director know the movie will reward rhythm, timing, and performance over exposition.
strengths.evidence: The donut banter, the comic insults, the British zombie's tea-and-bollocks routine, and the final 'Cool powers, dude' button.

whats_special.headline: SINON has a sharp commercial lane: a retro-futurist workplace action-comedy where a terrified office clerk is forced into a monster-killing unit and discovers he may be the most dangerous weapon in the room. The script’s biggest asset is how cleanly it packages world, tone, and ensemble into one sellable engine — bureaucratic absurdity on the surface, crowd-pleasing creature action underneath.

lead_characters.name: Francis Booker
lead_characters.hook: Francis is a frightened, sarcastic office drone whose whole identity is built around staying out of the blast radius. He starts as the guy annotating death tolls in a cubicle and ends up the one person in the room who can erase a monster, which gives him a built-in contradiction: the least field-ready person in the building may be the most consequential.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Jesse Eisenberg in The Social Network — a fast, defensive verbal rhythm masking panic and intelligence, with a late-story pivot into authority. Actors who want a role that starts as comic anxiety and ends as a power reveal will chase this.

lead_characters.name: Doreen
lead_characters.hook: Doreen is the hard-edged boss who speaks like she has already made peace with everyone dying on company time. She is all command voice and dry contempt on the surface, but the way she handles Francis and the team suggests a leader who knows exactly how much chaos she can afford to tolerate.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the command-and-control showcase of Jodie Foster in The Silence of the Lambs — a character whose authority is the performance, with intelligence and pressure living in every line. Mid-career dramatic actresses who can carry steel, wit, and institutional power will want this role.

lead_characters.name: Ploy
lead_characters.hook: Ploy is a bass-blasting chaos agent with a flirtatious mouth and a fighter's instincts, the kind of teammate who treats danger like a social event. She is funny, reckless, and weirdly perceptive, which makes her the first person to clock that Francis is lying to himself.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kinetic, scene-stealing territory of Jennifer Lawrence in The Hunger Games — a character who can swing from comic swagger to emotional clarity without losing momentum. Actors who want a role built on physical confidence, banter, and sudden sincerity will chase it.

lead_characters.name: Hal
lead_characters.hook: Hal is a swaggering bruiser who performs invincibility as a lifestyle choice. He talks like a war story never ends, laughs when people laugh at him, and turns every room into a contest of masculine volume, which makes him both funny and dangerous to underestimate.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the swagger-and-self-mythology lane of Brad Pitt in Snatch — a role where the joke is the character's confidence, but the actor still gets to sell physicality and charm. Performers with strong comic timing and a taste for larger-than-life bravado will want it.

lead_characters.name: Clara
lead_characters.hook: Clara is a coke-fueled sharpshooter with old-school gangster energy and zero interest in behaving like a professional. She is horny, volatile, funny, and lethal, which makes her feel like she wandered in from a different decade and decided to stay for the violence.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the feral charisma showcase of Margot Robbie in Birds of Prey — a role that lets an actor play volatility, seduction, and physical comedy in one package. Actors who want a loud, dangerous, highly quotable part will chase Clara.

lead_characters.name: Toast
lead_characters.hook: Toast is a sentient robot with the patience of a spreadsheet and the contempt of a machine that has seen too much flesh. The character's deadpan precision and literal-minded insults make him the team's coldest comic instrument, but the action beats also let him function as a tactical operator.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the dry, precision-comedy territory of Alan Tudyk in Resident Alien — a nonhuman role where the performance lives in timing, posture, and verbal exactitude. Voice performers or physical-comedy specialists who want to create a memorable character through rhythm and attitude will chase it.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to make action feel like office satire with teeth.
director_appeal.fit_profile: Second-feature or established indie-genre directors who already know how to stage dialogue-driven scenes and then pay them off with clean, readable action. The material rewards directors who care about comic timing, ensemble blocking, and building a world where bureaucracy and violence sit in the same frame.
director_appeal.detail: The movie gives a director a chance to control tone through performance and production design rather than scale, which is ideal for someone trying to make a calling-card genre feature. It also offers a very clear visual grammar — cubicles, briefing rooms, retro gear, and a London night chase — that lets a director show range without needing tentpole spectacle.

buyer_appeal.detail: The ensemble can be cast from strong working actors rather than name-dependent stars, with Francis as the only role that really needs a breakout lead to sell the transformation. The contained office footprint and one major creature-action set piece make it a clean fit for streamers and genre buyers who want a marketable concept without a sprawling effects bill.

considerations.area: Francis's power reveal is carried by one mechanism.
considerations.detail: The hot dog trigger is memorable and funny, and the reveal lands cleanly in the London fight. A next pass could consider seeding that logic a little earlier in the office material so the final payoff feels even more inevitable when the watch hits 95.

considerations.area: The opening dream image can do more work.
considerations.detail: The ruined college field, the cracked glasses, and the nosebleed are striking, but the sequence currently reads as a mood-forward prologue before the office world takes over. One direction would be to connect that image more directly to Francis's anomaly or the mission stakes so the opening functions as both atmosphere and story engine.

considerations.area: The team chemistry is strongest when it collides.
considerations.detail: The banter is already lively, and the movie gets a lift whenever Francis is forced to bounce off Ploy, Clara, Hal, and Toast in the same stretch. A future pass could foreground one or two sharper relationship turns inside the mission so the ensemble feels even more like a machine, not just a lineup.

considerations.area: The London sequence is the main production lift.
considerations.detail: The night exterior fight, rooftop coverage, creature regeneration, and weapon effects are the biggest spend drivers in the script. The contained office material is economical, so the cleanest simplification lever would be to protect the office footprint and keep the action geography as concentrated as possible around the street, alley, and one rooftop.
